title: 2026 Season Power Rankings
subtitle: Pre-Week 8 board, post-waivers. A four-way logjam at 5-2 after Hyper's 60-point Blake Cashman bomb knocked off Pocket, the Eddies won five straight and flipped Tyler Warren, Bryce Young and $11 to Substation for George Pickens and Frankie Luvu, and the Goats fell off the bus by two points. Doubtpfizer erupted for 311.5 to take the kitty, the Dongers finally got Win No. 1, Substation emptied its wallet ($21) on KC Concepcion, and the HOU/NO/NYG/SF byes park Fred Warner, Malik Nabers, George Kittle, CMC and Will Anderson Jr.
method: W/L + win quality + roster ceiling + FAAB + pedigree + sit/start + trades; PF is evidence, not the ranking.

rankings.blurb: Juice: still No. 1, still on the bus, and still leading the WU in PF at 1940.0—157.5 clear of second-place Doubtpfizer. Trey McBride dropped 40 (top TE of Week 7), Jared Goff had 27 and CeeDee Lamb posted 24 in a 234 that only lost because Blake Cashman went nuclear. Then Kellen shipped Malik Washington and $10 to TTAB for Dane Belton, spent $3 on Josh Hines-Allen on waivers, and still holds the fattest wallet in the league at $85. Junk: the five-game heater is dead, the IDP managed just 111, and Will Anderson Jr. followed a 2 with a 5 before heading into Houston's Week 8 bye alongside Tyler Shough and Woody Marks. Saquon Barkley, Jaylen Waddle and Rashid Shaheed are all parked in IR slots. The SPD's visit next with a top-four defense and a chip on their shoulder.

Juice: five straight wins after an 0-2 start, second in the 5-2 logjam at 1744.0 PF, and survived the bus cut by two points over the Goats behind a 137-point defense (Fred Warner 33, Jordyn Brooks 23, Evan Williams 20). Then the front office struck Tuesday night, sending Tyler Warren, Bryce Young and $11 to Substation for George Pickens and Commanders green-dot LB Frankie Luvu, before grabbing Bills safety Cole Bishop for $4 on Wednesday morning ($34 left). Trevor Lawrence is back off bye to run the show with Pickens and Garrett Wilson. Junk: the Week 7 offense put up 68.5 (Coker 1, Bourne 3, Wilson 4), Warner and Cameron Skattebo are on the SF/NYG byes, and Breece Hall (quad) is still questionable. A trip to hot Ultron—and a reunion with Rhamondre Stevenson—is next.

Juice: Jayden Daniels is back from the Commanders' bye, the 143-point IDP unit (Quay Walker 31, Drue Tranquill 23, Minkah Fitzpatrick 22, Aidan Hutchinson 21) never blinked, and 246.5 kept LAB safely on the bus with $56 left after a $5 Greg Dulcich pickup. Fourth in PF at 1732.0 and second-lowest PA in the league. Junk: Remember last week's warning not to lose to 0-6 Drummond or the WU would bring it up at the draft? Welp. The offense laid a 103.5 (Isaiah Likely 4.5, Tyler Allgeier 8, Carnell Tate 10) and handed the Dongers their first win of the year. C.J. Stroud and Likely hit the HOU/NYG byes, and Mike Evans and Jeremiyah Love remain in IR slots. The 5-2 Goats visit in a heavyweight showdown.

Juice: still tied atop the standings at 5-2 with the lowest PA in the league (1471.5) and the third-biggest wallet at $64 after adding Mark Andrews for $0. Bucky Irving (32), Quincy Williams (32), Keisean Nixon (22) and Josh Jacobs (20) kept them in a five-point game. Junk: one five-point loss to Saltese (208.5–203.5) cost the Goats the game, sole possession of first place, and their bus seat by exactly two points behind the Eddies. Patrick Mahomes (4), Derrick Henry (7) and DK Metcalf (7) tanked the offense to 98.5, and Week 8 byes wipe out George Kittle, Marvin Harrison, Danielle Hunter, Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller—while active LB Arvell Reese is on the Giants' bye too. A road trip to 5-2 LAB is a brutal spot to be shorthanded.

Juice: alone in fifth at 4-3, still riding the bus, and the most aggressive week in the league. Jack Campbell (26), Tykee Smith (26) and Malik Nabers (24) beat the Slumlords 222–195, then Nate shipped Demario Davis and Brian Branch to TTAB for Eagles LB Zack Baun, flipped George Pickens and Frankie Luvu to the Eddies for Tyler Warren, Bryce Young and $11, and immediately blew all $21 of his reload on KC Concepcion plus $0 grabs for Austin Booker, Tyjae Spears, Chris Godwin and Makai Lemon. Junk: the wallet is now at $0, Brock Purdy, Malik Nabers and Kaden Elliss are all on Week 8 byes, and newly acquired Tyler Warren (groin) sits in an IR slot next to Alec Pierce and Spears. Bryce Young starts against Green Bay on Thursday night, and 3-4 Hyper is waiting.

Juice: 311.5! Kyle printed the fourth 300-point score of the season, took home the Week 7 kitty, made it two straight wins, and vaulted to second in the entire league in PF (1782.5). Alex Singleton erupted for 53 to headline a 178-point IDP unit alongside Nakobe Dean (30), DeMarvion Overshown (30) and Kamari Lassiter (26), while Dak Prescott (28), Braelon Allen (27) and Colston Loveland (24.5) paced the offense. Still on the bus and still sitting on $75 after spending $10 on Kyler Gordon ($5), Kaelon Black ($3) and Nohl Williams ($2). Junk: the 1911.0 PA is still the worst in the WU by 104.5, and the HOU/SF byes park CMC, Nico Collins, Kamari Lassiter, Kaelon Black and Reed Blankenship while Rashee Rice stays in an IR slot. The Slumlords come to town.

Juice: knocked off No. 1 Pocket 252–234 behind Blake Cashman's 60-point masterpiece—the second-highest single-player game in the WU all season—plus Nick Bolton (27), Payton Wilson (23), Amon-Ra St. Brown (30) and Luther Burden (29). Third in PF at 1771.5, still on the bus, Justin Herbert and Travis Hunter are back from their Week 7 byes, and Jacob dropped $13 on waivers for Jacory Croskey-Merritt ($9) and a Micah Parsons stash ($4). Junk: the wallet is down to $12, St. Brown and Emeka Egbuka carry injury tags in active slots, and Nick Bosa, Jalen Pitre and Jaylin Noel are on the SF/HOU byes. Hosting 4-3 Substation is a prime chance to get back to .500.

Juice: Zay Flowers (33), Tee Higgins (32) and Henry To'oTo'o (31) carried a 236 that comfortably survived the bus cut, and Ryan added safety Grant Delpit for $3 ($44 left). Fifth in PF (1663.5) and one of the seven teams still alive on the bus. Junk: three straight losses have buried a top-five scoring roster at 3-4, the tight end slot remains a black hole after Juwan Johnson's 2, A.J. Brown posted a 7, and Houston/New Orleans byes take out To'oTo'o, Azeez Al-Shaair and Johnson while Davante Adams, Zaire Franklin and Nathan Landman sit in IR slots. Next up is a road trip to angry 5-2 Pocket.

Juice: dropped 255.5—the highest losing score of Week 7 and the fifth-highest score in the league—which buried Saltese (208.5) on Last Ride and put TTAB in the driver's seat for Week 8 against the Goats. Josh Allen and Stefon Diggs return from bye, and Chase reshaped the roster with three deals: flipping Zack Baun to Substation for Brian Branch and Demario Davis, trading Ashton Jeanty to Ultron for DeVonta Smith and Dillon Thieneman, and dealing Dane Belton to Pocket for Malik Washington and $10 in fresh FAAB, plus adding Ryan Flournoy for $0. Junk: ran straight into Doubtpfizer's 311.5 buzzsaw, the defense gave up a 154.5 offensive gem by scoring just 101, and DeVonta Smith, Divine Deablo and Andrew Wingard are in IR slots. A winnable trip to Morningside awaits.

Juice: snapped a four-game skid by knocking off the 5-1 Goats 208.5–203.5 and bouncing them off the bus! Jamien Sherwood (29), Tre Tucker (27), Matthew Stafford (22) and Dre Greenlaw (22) carried the day, Omarion Hampton is back from the Chargers' bye, Luke flipped DeVonta Smith and Mack Wilson to Ultron for Bhayshul Tuten, and Wednesday waivers brought in Dee Winters ($4), Colby Parkinson ($1), Ty Okada ($1) and Brandon Cisse ($0). Junk: that same 208.5 got smoked by TTAB's 255.5 on Last Ride, ending Saltese's re-entry run for good. Chase Young, Dre Greenlaw and David Montgomery hit the NO/SF/HOU byes, and Aaron Jones sits on IR. Hosting the Dongers is a rematch with JSN.

Juice: two straight wins and the third-highest score of Week 7 at 269.5! Kendal Daniels (44) and new Giants green-dot LB Micah McFadden (36) spearheaded a 136 IDP, while Caleb Williams (31), newly acquired Ashton Jeanty (22), D'Andre Swift (21) and Rhamondre Stevenson (22) cooked for 133.5 on offense. Foye Oluokun is back from the Jaguars' bye, and Brian added CJ Allen and Jake Ferguson for $0. Junk: only $2 in FAAB left, McFadden heads into the Giants' Week 8 bye, and Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Kyle Monangai are all parked on IR. The 5-2 Eddies come to town for a Stevenson revenge sequel.

Juice: Drake Maye (35), Jahmyr Gibbs (25) and Quinshon Judkins (24) won the offensive half against Substation, James Cook returns from the Bills' bye to reunite a lethal three-headed RB room with Gibbs and Judkins, and zero starters are on Week 8 byes. Junk: the defense that dropped 160 in Week 6 cratered to 85 (Budda Baker 3, Devon Witherspoon 6, Maxx Crosby 11) in a 222–195 loss, Kalif Raymond goose-egged (0), the PA is second-worst in the league (1786.5), and the FAAB wallet is at $0. Visiting red-hot Doubtpfizer (311.5) is a tough place to stop the bleeding.

Juice: Bobby Okereke (31), Jessie Bates (29), Demetrius Knight (23) and Ollie Gordon (26) kept Morningside within 13 points of the Eddies, and Ladd Herbert's Chargers are back from bye. Junk: three straight losses, the Week 7 league floor at 192.5, and dead last in season PF (1449.0—79.5 behind 13th-place Ultron). The WR room went Justin Jefferson 8, Keenan Allen 8, Jordan Addison 4 and Xavier Worthy 4, Lamar Jackson carries an injury tag, Pete Werner and Deebo Samuel are on the NO/SF byes, and Derwin James sits on IR with only $8 FAAB left. TTAB visits next.

Juice: THE DONGERS HAVE WON A FOOTBALL GAME! After an 0-6 start, Gavin dropped 278—the second-highest score in the league—to knock off 5-1 LAB behind a league-best 160 offense: Tony Pollard (44), newly acquired JSN (37), Joe Burrow (36) and T.J. Hockenson (16), plus Christian Elliss (33) and Xavier McKinney (20) on defense. Their 1565.0 PF now outscores both Morningside and Ultron. Junk: still 1-6 with $1 left, Chris Olave and Jevon Holland hit the NO/NYG byes, and D.J. Moore, Ladd McConkey and Zach Allen carry injury tags. Next up is a trip to Saltese—the team that just traded them JSN.
